sections.html:
Bloomington is the McLean County seat in central Illinois, covering 27.24 square miles. The count was 78,680 in 2020 and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 78,804. Median value of owner homes is $203,300, 61.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, median gross rent is $1,050 and the average commute is 16.8 minutes.

Employers such as State Farm and Illinois State University in neighboring Normal supply a steady stream of local buyers. Many shoppers tour houses in both towns on the same weekend, so check recent sales in each before pricing.

Two public districts cover the city. Bloomington Public Schools District 87 serves the interior with Bloomington High School, Bloomington Junior High and six elementary schools. Growth pushed the city well into McLean County Unit District No. 5, which runs Normal Community High School and Normal Community West High School. A small part of the city lies in Olympia Community Unit School District 16, and Central Catholic High School is a private option.

Attendance lines do not follow city limits, so look up the exact district for your street before the listing goes live. Families ask this first at a showing.

Landlords in the city must register each residential rental and hold a Certificate of Inspection before a unit is rented or leased. When you sell a rental, these rules decide what the next owner starts with.

Bloomington rental program costs
Fee or taxAmount
Registration, per building$65
Added per rental unit, buildings of three or more units$5
Follow-up inspection$100
Missed inspection$75
Short Term Rental Tax, stays under 30 days6.0 percent
  • The first inspection is included in the registration fee, and each owned condo needs its own registration.
  • A registration lasts through December 31 and does not pass to a new owner, so the buyer files a fresh one.
  • Inspectors give owners at least 15 days' notice and check the building against the International Property Maintenance Code, the Fire Code and other ordinances.
  • A building rated fair may be required to post a $5,000 letter of credit or pledged account until it receives a passing rating.
  • Violations not fixed by the reinspection date lead to a court appearance and possible court costs.

Hosts who rent for short stays remit the tax by the 25th of the next month and owe a 5 percent penalty if they pay late. They also register the unit every year in the rental program. Clear any unpaid tax or open inspection item before you close.

Investors who pay cash will often accept a tenant-occupied building, or one with violations, in its current state. That can spare you a round of repairs and reinspection. The city's rules still follow the building to its next owner, so put in writing who handles reinspection after closing.

Anything tied to your time as owner, such as unpaid fees or a pending court date, is yours to clear first. Ask the city what is open on the address, and file inspection reports and any passing rating with your sale papers.

The McLean County Clerk's office handles recording at 115 E. Washington Street, Bloomington. Its Predictable Recording Fee Schedule, effective July 1, 2023, sets a standard document at $61.00. Documents exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee, such as government filings and powers of attorney, are $41.00, and a non-standard document is $75.00.

A document counts as non-standard if it uses legal- or ledger-size paper or has six or more PIN or related-document references. Recorded documents must be originals or certified copies. Certified copies cost $18.00 and additional copies $1.00 per page. The recording phone is (309) 888-5170.

The state transfer declaration and any transfer tax come on top of the recording fee. Your title company collects them at the table. Request an itemized settlement statement a few days early and check each line.

You have 30 days from the publication date shown for your township to file an assessment complaint with the Board of Review, and a late complaint will not be heard. The county posts each township's publication and deadline dates in a table, and the Board of Review office is at (309) 888-5132. For 2026 the equalization factors were 1.0534 for the Bloomington township and 1.0385 for the City of Bloomington township.

Non-farm complaints go on Form PTAX-230. Values rest on market activity in the three years before January 1 of the assessment year, and a multiplier brings the statutory assessment to 33.33 percent. The City of Bloomington Township Assessor holds property record cards and an online lookup, which helps when you want to see how neighbors are assessed.

sections.h2: Where a buyer's questions usually land
sections.html: Bloomington buyers who shop with a mortgage tend to ask about three things: the school district, the property tax bill, and whether the building is a registered rental. Having those answers on one sheet makes your house easier to say yes to. Add the township, the last tax amount and any inspection rating, so the buyer's agent does not have to chase you.

Taxes are the part of a Bloomington closing most likely to surprise a seller who has not looked at a bill lately. Pull your current statement and note both installment amounts, and tell your title company if you hold an exemption.

Before closing, call the County Treasurer for installment dates and a payoff figure. Which installments are already paid drives the proration on your statement. If you appeal, keep the Board of Review decision with your records so a buyer can see the outcome.

Without a buyer's lender in the picture the timeline shortens, yet recording and taxes work the same. A typical order looks like this.

  • Collect the deed, newest tax bill, rental registration, inspection reports and repair receipts.
  • Find out which school district and township assessor your address falls under.
  • Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer.
  • Send your title company the buyer's details so the statement is drafted early.
  • At the table, read the recording fee, state declaration and any transfer tax line by line, then sign the deed that goes to the County Clerk.

Tell buyers early if the house is empty or has tenants. An as-is purchaser prices the condition in, and an honest list of known problems saves time. Leases can move the closing date, so show a copy at your first conversation.

faqs.q: Can a new owner use the previous owner's Bloomington rental registration?
faqs.a: No, it does not carry over. A buyer who wants to rent the building registers it fresh, pays the fee and passes inspection.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in McLean County?
faqs.a: A standard document is $61.00 and a non-standard one is $75.00 under the July 1, 2023 schedule. Phone the County Clerk to confirm before you send payment.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a McLean County assessment?
faqs.a: Thirty days from your township's publication date. Late complaints are not heard, and the county posts the dates each year.

faqs.q: Is the short-term rental tax applied to every Bloomington short-term stay?
faqs.a: Stays under 30 days carry the 6.0 percent tax. Hosts on a listing site still register each property and file monthly certification forms.

faqs.q: Does a cash sale remove the need to fix rental violations in Bloomington?
faqs.a: The rules follow the building, though a cash buyer may take it as-is and handle repairs and reinspection later. Clear fees or court matters from your ownership first, and get the terms in writing.
